items.title: StackScope – I crawled over 40k indie launches to see what they ship

It watches launches from Product Hunt, Show HN, and PeerPush, then crawls the public site behind each one. The goal is to show what people actually launched with: hosting, frameworks, analytics, DNS, security headers, legal pages, AI-builder signals, and other public clues. I started building it because most stack-detection sites look at the web as a whole. I was more interested in the current indie launch scene: what people are choosing right now, at the point they first put something in public. excerpt_i18n.en: Over the past six months, the "lobster fever" sparked by OpenClaw has plunged the AI community into collective euphoria: AI writes code for you, replies to emails, and even takes over devices, as if the countdown to "replacing humans" has already begun. Nvidia's Jensen Huang called it "one of the most important software releases ever," adding fuel to the frenzy. But as the bubble slightly deflates, the IoT industry is left with awkward cracks on the beach. An accidental email deletion in a company's lab, a source code leak at another firm, and the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology's March advisory on preventing security risks from OpenClaw ("Lobster") open-source intelligent agents all remind us: when general-purpose agents pursue "omniscience and omnipotence," they often come with the risk of losing control. The 2026 FIFA World Cup in the USA, Canada, and Mexico is approaching. Today, Qianwen held the launch salon for its first football prediction AI assistant. Users are invited to predict match scores to earn points. Participants can not only help Qianwen donate football fields to rural schools but also have the chance to win a cash prize of 10,000 yuan.  

Qianwen Launches Football Prediction AI Assistant  
The first football prediction AI assistant has been launched, integrating big data such as weather and terrain. This is the first World Cup where AI fully participates in match predictions. Qianwen’s football prediction AI assistant is now open to all users. Cheng Fei, head of Qianwen’s AI prediction products, explained that the assistant is trained on vast amounts of big data, including historical data, player statistics, injury conditions, and even terrain data of the USA, Canada, and Mexico, as well as weather data during match periods.  

Using the example of the group stage match between Norway and Senegal on June 22, Cheng Fei noted that Norway, with world-class striker Erling Haaland, seems likely to win. However, Qianwen predicted a 1-1 draw.  

“The reason for this prediction is the weather,” Cheng Fei explained. “Since this World Cup is hosted by three countries, matches may face completely different weather conditions. Qianwen considers factors such as temperature, humidity, kick-off time, and the typical playing environments of both teams.” Similarly, the opening match between Mexico and South Africa is also influenced by weather and altitude. Qianwen predicts a Mexican victory, not only due to home-field advantage but also because of the special factor of Mexico City’s altitude of over 2,200 meters.
